sections.summary: Labour productivity grew 2.5% yearly from 2016 to 2024, while real mean income grew 1.3%, and output per worker outpaced major economies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Overall, labour productivity has grown by 2.5% per year from 2016 to 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But over the same period, real mean income only grew at 1.3% per year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: From 2016 to 2024, according to the International Labour Organization (ILO), Singapore's output per worker grew 2.3% per year, outstripping major economies, such as the United States (US) at 1.6%, Israel at 1.6%, Hong Kong at 1.3%, Korea at 1.3% and Switzerland at 1.1%.

sections.label: Pricing state land at development cost
sections.summary: The proposition is that Singapore should stop treating market land value as a natural price for every socially productive use of land, tested by a university-centred special zone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, the proposition: Singapore should stop treating market land value as a natural price for every socially productive use of land.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And the test: a university-centred special zone where state land is priced at development cost rather than market scarcity value.

sections.label: Special zone around NTU
sections.summary: The bargain has four parts, and a special zone surrounding NTU should be created where state land is charged as cost recovery and returns come from companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The bargain has four parts: a place to live, near where the work and the research happen; at a price a starting salary can carry, in service of something the country needs – more local enterprise and R&D – with the upside staying with the risk-takers and a say in the rules.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: What we should create a special zone surrounding Nanyang Technological University (NTU), where the state land is charged as cost recovery rather than market scarcity value and takes its returns in the companies that grow there, rather than rent.

sections.label: Development cost of completed flats

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Land was 59% of the cost of a flat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Second, the Johor Zone Agreement was signed in January 2025.

sections.label: NTU and co-living room rents
sections.summary: NTU rooms cost about $412 to $657 monthly, while co-living rooms start at $1,800 to $2,000, roughly 30% below the usual rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: At NTU this academic year, a non-air-conditioned double room costs about $412 a month, and an air-conditioned single room about $657.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under the co-living scheme announced in late July this year, under the SG Youth plan, a room starts at $1,800 a month at 1925 Quarters; $1,950 at Coliwoo Boon Lay and $2,000 at Coliwoo Lutheran, before utilities and deposits – roughly 30% below the usual rate, with operators absorbing the difference.

sections.label: 500 square foot unit cost
sections.summary: A 500 square foot unit at $200 per square foot, amortised over 10 years at 5%, comes to about $1,061 monthly, or $380 a head.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A 500 square foot unit at $200 a square foot – above the construction cost implied by the Government's own 2022 figures, so, it is a conservative assumption and not a hopeful one – if you put three people in it and amortise over 10 years at 5%, it comes out to about $1,061 a month, or $2.12 per square foot, roughly $380 a head, with a sinking fund in.

sections.label: JTC leases and zone proposals
sections.summary: JTC lets land on its own lease terms, and the speaker proposes lifting URA's campus use cap and hastening visa decisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: JTC let its land on contracts it writes itself – rent formulas, renewal test, quotas, carve outs, occupancy covenants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These are lease terms and not statutes with already existing latitude.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We should lift the Urban Redevelopment Authority's (URA's) planning circular, capping non-academic use of a campus at 5% of floor area or 30,000 square metres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We can hasten visa decisions for deep-tech researchers and for the people the enterprises need, and aim to have every major decision in such a zone made within two weeks.

sections.label: Oriza Holdings investment arm
sections.summary: The zone's state-owned investment arm, Oriza Holdings, was incorporated in 2001 and manages about US$14 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The zone grew its own investment arm, Oriza Holdings – state-owned, controlled by the Parks Administration Committee, incorporated in 2001, with about US$14 billion under management today.

sections.label: Zone proposal and threefold ask
sections.summary: The speaker asks for a zone around NTU, a new restricted land use category, and a zone authority taking stakes in enterprises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Speaker, the zone is one bounded, reversible way to try on available land at a price that takes nothing from the reserves, with land prices outside the zone exactly the way they were – a way to make more Singaporeans involved in enterprise and R&D, and not only employees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, the ask is threefold: a zone around NTU; a new use category for restricted tenure, non-tradable, mixed housing and enterprise land, valued as the restricted interest it is; and a zone authority that runs its own operations and takes stakes in the enterprises it grows.

sections.label: WP Motion on future economy
sections.summary: The WP moved a Motion to create an economy of the future, shifting from an MNC-centric model to an SME-focused one.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Singaporeans deserve serious answers; and serious answers are what the WP will provide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: That is why we have moved this Motion to create an economy of the future that works for all.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I cannot agree more that we need both dynamic local companies and opportunities for businesses to succeed, which is why my contribution to this debate will focus on how we can wean ourselves away from a top-down foreign investment, reliant multinational corporation- (MNC-) centric economic model; and instead build a bottom-up domestic capital led small and medium enterprise- (SME-) focused one.

sections.label: Institutions, taxes, property rights, civil service
sections.summary: Emphasis on quality institutions, low taxes, property rights, rule of law and a high functioning civil service raised per capita income from about $1,600 at Independence to more than $121,000 today.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We also placed emphasis on quality institutions and attractive low tax climate, respect for property rights and rule of law and a high functioning civil service.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We fired on all these cylinders, which brought us famously from a per capita income of around $1,600 at Independence; to more than $121,000 today – a massive increase by any stretch of the imagination.

sections.label: Productivity growth lagging
sections.summary: A known design flaw in relentlessly accumulating inputs to production has left Singapore lagging in productivity growth.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Perhaps the most damning drawback is a known design flaw in the relentless pursuit of accumulating inputs to production, we have lagged in productivity growth.

sections.label: Shift from MNCs to SMEs
sections.summary: Singapore must evolve away from reliance on foreign MNCs toward SMEs, shifting from tax competition, undervalued exchange rates and wooing footloose MNCs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For starters, we must evolve away from our traditional reliance on foreign MNCs as a driver of our growth and pivot toward SMEs as our homegrown economic engine.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While the ESR speaks about both, it betrays, somewhat, an implicit bias toward the former.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We need a conscious shift from not too much fixation with tax competition and undervalued exchange rate and the wooing of footloose MNCs.

sections.label: SMEs share of economy
sections.summary: SMEs account for 99 of 100 registered enterprises and employ seven of 10 Singaporean workers, but contribute only half of the economy's value added.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Yet, while SMEs account for 99 out of 100 registered enterprises here and provide jobs for seven out of 10 Singaporean workers, they currently only contribute to half of the economy's value added.

sections.label: SMEs low productivity
sections.summary: SMEs struggle with low levels of productivity, which the Government itself has explicitly acknowledged.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Most notably, SMEs struggle with low levels of productivity, something that the Government itself has explicitly acknowledged.

sections.label: R&D pivot and funding
sections.summary: The ESR talks about R&D but does not underscore the pivot's importance, while the Prime Minister's Office announced a $37 billion commitment to research, innovation and enterprise funding over five years.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The ESR talks about R&D, but it does not underscore the importance of this pivot.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I note that the Prime Minister's Office announced last year a $37 billion commitment to research, innovation and enterprise funding over the next five years.

sections.label: Corporate R&D tax incentives
sections.summary: Tax incentives for corporate R&D allow up to 400% deduction for the first $400,000 of qualifying expenditures yearly, plus up to 100% Refundable Investment Credit.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To be fair, tax incentives for corporations to undertake R&D are already very generous, with up to 400% deduction for the first $400,000 of qualifying expenditures every assessment year, supplemented more recently by up to 100% in Refundable Investment Credit.

sections.label: Domestic enterprises' R&D spending share
sections.summary: Domestic enterprises account for half of the economy's value-added R&D spending but only $1 of every $5.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Despite being half of our economy's value-added R&D spending by domestic enterprises account for only $1 of every $5.

sections.label: Cap on annual rent increases
sections.summary: One strategy is to cap the maximum yearly rent increase at the historical annual increase of about 3%, limiting the rate not the level.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: One simple strategy is to cap the maximum quantum that rents may increase every year to the historical increase of about 3% annually.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This is a limit on the rate, not the level.

sections.label: SME internship participation and German approach
sections.summary: In 2024 ITE supplied 1,300 students and autonomous universities 800, with around 300 firms, under 1% of registered SMEs, joining such programmes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In 2024, the Institute of Technical Education (ITE) supplied 1,300 students while autonomous universities sent 800.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Around 300 firms have joined such programmes, which are less than 1% of registered SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This can be insurmountable for smaller companies with limited resources and understanding of how to go about doing so.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It may be better to take a cue from the German approach, where more than one in 10 companies participate in their equivalent programme, by expanding the scope of potential applicants, allowing interns to be hired using SkillsFuture funds and accepting simpler application criteria from SME employers.

sections.label: Grants paired with skills transfer
sections.summary: Larger grants should be paired with a clear proposal and timetable for skills transfer, including possibly sunsetting foreign Employment Passes after a designated duration.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Larger grants in particular should be paired with a clear proposal and timetable for ensuring skills transfer, including the possibility of a sunset of foreign Employment Passes after a designated duration if no additional transfer is taking place.

sections.label: Not a wholesale model overhaul
sections.summary: The call is not for a wholesale overhaul of the GLC-heavy, MNC-led and foreign capital-reliant model, which has served us well to date.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: To be clear, what I am calling for is not a wholesale overhaul of our GLC-heavy, MNC-led and foreign capital-reliant model, which has to date served us well.

sections.label: Shift to homegrown medium-sized firms
sections.summary: Calls for policy and institutional shifts placing small and medium-sized firms at the heart of Singapore's economic model, away from large foreign MNCs and GLCs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: No modern economy, much less a globalised one, like ours, operates without due attention to international players.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: But what I am calling for are policy and institutional shifts that will usher in a changed mindset for how we should view our homegrown companies in an already wealthy, advanced economy.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: The shift will place small, but especially, medium-sized firms at the beating heart of our nation's economic model, away from the interests of large foreign-based MNCs or even our GLC behemoths.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: By destroying, we will create simultaneously an economy ready for the 21st century.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
sentences.text: The Government can do this to help local enterprises internationalise through market access platforms, financing support, overseas networks, talent development and stronger partnerships with regional governments and businesses.

sections.summary: The passage argues for supporting local enterprises, embracing AI to expand human capability, and ensuring Singaporeans benefit domestically while remaining a global trusted hub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
sentences.text: We must strengthen our role as a global trusted hub and we must ensure that every Singaporean has a fair chance to contribute and benefit from the future economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui

sections.label: State land ownership and ESR report
sections.summary: The passage states the state owns about 90% of Singapore's land and that land is not mentioned in the ESR report's 32 recommendations.

sentences.text: The state owns some 90% of the land in Singapore and it is by a wide margin the biggest landlord in the country.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In fact, even as economists often identify the key factors of production, being land, labour, capital and entrepreneurship, there is not a single mention of land in the 32 recommendations of the ESR report, even as the report itself had acknowledged that land, energy and demographic constraints are expected to tighten.

sections.label: Land costs share of development expenditure
