sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As a local C-suite member of one of Asia's largest real estate groups has shared in the past, in Singapore, land costs now form roughly 70% of total project development expenditure, up from just 4% in the 1980s for Raffles City.

sections.label: Reserve price and unawarded tender sites
sections.summary: The passage states the reserve price is pegged to 85% of estimated market value and that 17 of 133 sites tendered from 2016 to 2021 were not awarded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In a reply to my Parliamentary Question in July 2021, the Minister for Law disclosed that the reserve price is pegged to 85% of the estimated market value assessed by the Chief Valuer's office; and that of the 133 sites launched for tender between 2016 and 2021, 17 were not awarded because the highest bids were deemed not reflective of the fair market value of the land.

sections.label: Site sold at higher rate
sections.summary: The passage states a site tendered and awarded in April 2015 was sold at $1.67 billion, or $943 per square foot per plot ratio, about two thirds higher than an earlier refused bid.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: When the site was eventually tended and awarded in April 2015, it was sold at $1.67 billion, or $943 per square foot per plot ratio, at a rate some two thirds higher than the bid the Government had earlier refused.

sections.label: Singapore household mortgage borrowing growth
sections.summary: Home loans are at least 70% of household liabilities in Singapore, and mortgage borrowing grew 5.8% year on year in Q1 this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Home loans make up at least 70% of total household liabilities in Singapore and mortgage borrowing grew 5.8% year on year in the first quarter of this year.

sections.label: Singapore workers living paycheck to paycheck
sections.summary: ADP Research found 60% of workers in Singapore were living paycheck to paycheck as of 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Moreover, according to ADP Research, 60% of workers in Singapore were living paycheck to paycheck as of 2024.

sections.label: Public rental option for Singaporeans
sections.summary: The speaker calls for a public rental option for young and middle-income Singaporeans with tenure-security and income-based rent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: My second call is therefore for a meaningful public rental option for young and middle-income Singaporeans with tenure-security and rent set with reference to income rather than market value.

sections.label: Compute as AI economy input
sections.summary: Compute is the scarce foundational input of the AI economy, and an Enterprise Compute Initiative was announced at Budget 2025 with up to $150 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In the AI economy, compute is to value creation what land was to the industrial economy, the scarce foundational input on which everything else is built.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We have made a start and I acknowledge that an Enterprise Compute Initiative was announced at Budget 2025 with up to $150 million of funding support.

sections.label: Land sales versus AI funding
sections.summary: Singapore extracts about $20 billion yearly in land sales proceeds but sets aside $150 million for compute and $1 billion over five years for AI research.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We extract some $20 billion in a single year in land sales proceeds also and yet, we are only setting aside $150 million for the digital land on which our own companies must build, and $1 billion over five years in overall national AI research.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And for all our first-place finishes in AI-readiness, only 4% of firms had embedded AI into core business processes by 2026, with adoption at 15% among SMEs, against 63% for larger firms.

sections.label: Policy options for compute access
sections.summary: Policy-makers can act by expanding compute access for startups and researchers and investing in shared training assets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Policy-makers have an important opportunity to act, such as through expanding access to compute for startups and researchers, and investing in shared training assets.

sections.label: Subsidised compute for local companies
sections.summary: A national compute programme should offer subsidised allocated capacity to local companies, especially SMEs and entrepreneurs, priced below market with published rates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Similarly, a national compute programme should offer a subsidised allocated capacity to local companies and particularly, SMEs and entrepreneurs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This will draw on capacity in which the state has an ownership interest, priced below market with a published rate card with tenure certainty and eligibility weighted towards local ownership and local value capture.

sections.label: Tax incentives for foreign investment
sections.summary: Singapore offers generous low tax incentives and corporate income tax as low as 5% instead of 17% to attract MNCs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Third, we do not apply this stinginess to foreign investment promotion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We extend generous low tax incentives and charge as low as 5% corporate income tax, instead of 17% to attract MNCs via a series of incentive schemes.

sections.label: Economic Strategy Review Committee report
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the committee's final report and supports the Motion, but says the vision stays on paper while the state maximises rent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I welcome the final recommendation report of the Economic Strategy Review Committee and I support that Motion moved by Mr Kenneth Tiong and Assoc Prof Jamus Lim.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But, as long as the state remains the most successful rent maximiser in our economy, the grand vision of this strategy will remain only on paper.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The hon Members Assoc Prof Lim and Mr Kenneth Tiong have tapped into a sentiment that some Singaporeans genuinely feel: some business owners feel the economy has grown harder to navigate; some SMEs feel squeezed by costs, including rents, by manpower, and they feel crowded out for business and funding opportunities by larger competition; some workers, including younger workers, wonder if opportunity for them is expanding as fast as the economy itself.

sections.label: Singapore's complementary strengths advantage
sections.summary: Singapore's advantage has been combining complementary strengths that reinforce one another into ecosystems creating more value.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Singapore's advantage has been our ability to combine complementary strengths that reinforce one another into ecosystems that create more value.

sections.label: EDB major investment approvals
sections.summary: When EDB approves a major investment it asks more than capital or jobs; in 2025 with Enterprise Singapore it generated 19 MNC-local partnership projects.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: When EDB approves a major investment, it is not simply asking how much capital will come or how many jobs will be created.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In 2025, working alongside Enterprise Singapore, EDB generated 19 MNC-local enterprise partnership projects.

sections.label: Constraints facing enterprises
sections.summary: The constraints are usually different: access to growth capital, cross-border management experience, technology transformation, overseas market networks, or risk appetite.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The constraints are usually different – access to growth capital, management with experience running operations across borders, or leading technology transformation, networks that open overseas markets, risk appetite.

sections.label: PSA global terminals and data
sections.summary: PSA operates over 70 terminals in 45 countries, and managing ports worldwide gives it a data advantage as competitive advantage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Today, it operates over 70 terminals across more than 180 locations in 45 countries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But the most valuable thing PSA has now is not simply a larger portfolio of terminals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Managing ports across the world's major trade routes gives PSA a unique view of global supply chains.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: By combining operational expertise with digital technologies, data, automation and AI to design solutions its customers cannot get from a single-port operator.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The data advantage, the capability, that is the competitive advantage.

sections.label: Singapore building future economy
sections.summary: Singapore succeeded by being useful to the world, and must build a future economy with opportunities for more Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Singapore never succeeded by asking the world to make room for us.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We succeeded by becoming useful, indispensable to it, even as the world changes around us.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Our task is now to continue to build an economy of the future where each reinforces the other, where the best companies, foreign or local, want to be.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: And to make sure more Singaporeans have the capability, the confidence and the opportunity to shape that future, to create value, to capture it and increasingly, to own it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So that every generation of Singaporeans begins with opportunities greater than the generation before.

sections.label: Autonomous university graduate employment rates
sections.summary: 88.9% of the 2025 autonomous university graduate cohort secured employment within six months, down from 91.2% in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Among autonomous- university graduates in the labour force, those who secured employment of any kind within six months of completing their final examinations amounted to 88.9% of the 2025 cohort, a slight drop from 91.2% in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It includes graduates in full-time permanent employment; but also, those in part-time, temporary or freelance work; those who have accepted a job that starts later; and those taking steps to start a business.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, those in full-time permanent employment amounted to 74.4% of the cohort last year, down from 79.4% the previous year.

sections.label: Private education graduate employment rates
sections.summary: Among surveyed fresh graduates from full-time external degree programmes at private education institutions, 78.9% secured employment and 46.9% were in full-time permanent employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Among surveyed fresh graduates from full-time external degree programmes at private education institutions, 78.9% secured employment and 46.9% were in full-time permanent employment.

sections.label: Fair Start Promise for youths
sections.summary: Exposure is not employment, so a "Fair Start Promise" is proposed as a national commitment to work towards a simple goal for youths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Exposure is useful, but exposure is not employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: And Mr Speaker, that is why I propose a "Fair Start Promise" to all our youths – a national commitment to work towards a simple goal.

sections.label: Fair Start Promise as SWDA mission
sections.summary: The Government should make fulfilling the "Fair Start Promise" a core mission of SWDA, with staged targets showing progress.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Government should make fulfilling the "Fair Start Promise" a core mission of SWDA, with staged targets that show whether Singapore is moving closer to the goal.

sections.label: Priority for ordinary entry-level jobs
sections.summary: Where an employer has real work that can develop a beginner, the priority should be that proper job.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: First, we should open more ordinary entry-level jobs to capable beginners, where an employer has real work that can develop a beginner through the ordinary course of employment, the priority should be that proper job.

sections.label: SWDA standards for verified competencies
sections.summary: The SWDA should establish standards for IHLs and employers to verify projects, internships, Work-Study stints and assessed competencies through the Careers and Skills Passport.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The SWDA should establish standards through which the institutes of higher learning (IHLs) and employers can verify substantial projects, internships, Work-Study learning stints and other assessed competencies through the Careers and Skills Passport.

sections.label: Apprenticeship framework and SWDA role
sections.summary: GRIT offers short traineeships, but sustained occupations need a proper apprenticeship framework, and SWDA should expand apprenticeship places meeting a common quality floor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: GRIT, for example, offers a three- to six-month allowance-based traineeship and can provide useful short-term experience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But where an occupation requires sustained, supervised practice over a longer period of time, we need a different, more well-developed route: a proper apprenticeship framework providing paid employment, full employee status, CPF, structured training and portable competences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: SWDA should identify occupations where employers need workers but beginners need sustained workplace training, and work with employers and sector bodies to expand apprenticeship places that meet a common quality floor.

sections.label: Support and procurement conditions
sections.summary: Support should be available where an employer creates a genuine additional job or apprenticeship that would not proceed without help, and procuring agencies can require proportionate commitment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Support should be available where an employer can show that they will create a genuine additional employee job or proper apprenticeship, and that the opening would not proceed on the same terms without help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Where workforce development is relevant to a substantial public contract, procuring agencies can require or recognise proportionate commitment to proper apprenticeships and genuine employee entry level roles.

sections.label: Recovering money for misrepresentation
sections.summary: Money should be recovered where an employer misrepresents the role or fails to provide the promised job, wages or development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Money should be recovered where an employer misrepresents the role or fails to provide the job, wages or development promised.

sections.label: Baseline, targets and six-month outcomes
sections.summary: The SWDA should publish a baseline and staged targets, and results must show how many young people remain without stable employment at six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The SWDA should publish a baseline and staged targets for those outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The results must also show how many young people remain without stable employment at the critical six-month mark, for how long and for what broad reasons.

sections.label: Skills-based hiring and apprenticeships
sections.summary: The three proposals are opening jobs to beginners with skills-based hiring, building paid apprenticeships and creating opportunities where public intervention changes hiring decisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The three proposals I suggested are the practical ways to move closer towards making that a reality: opening existing jobs to capable beginners with skills-based hiring, building proper paid apprenticeships and creating additional opportunities where public intervention changes the calculus and hiring decision for any employer.

sections.label: Geopolitical tensions and protectionism
sections.summary: Livelihood fundamentals cannot be disrupted, amid geopolitical tensions, a multi-polar world, rising protectionism and supply chains reconfigured along political lines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The fundamental of our livelihood cannot be disrupted or changed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We live in an era of heightened geopolitical tensions and a multi-polar world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Countries are turning inwards, protectionism is rising, supply chains are being re-configured along political lines.

sections.label: Expanding free trade agreements
sections.summary: Singapore must expand its network of free trade agreements with as many countries as possible, including emerging markets, not just big economies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To do this, we must expand our network of free trade agreements (FTAs).

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We must pursue FTAs with as many countries as possible, not just big economies but also, emerging markets.

sections.label: Grants to derisk internationalisation
sections.summary: The Government should enhance grants and financial support to derisk internationalisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Government should enhance grants – as what we have seen before – and financial support to derisk internationalisation.

sections.label: SMEs share of enterprises and workforce
sections.summary: SMEs make up 99% of Singapore's enterprises and employ about two-thirds of its workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: SMEs make up 99% of our enterprises and employ about two-thirds of our workforce.

sections.label: Sustainability and green hub measures
sections.summary: As Singapore aims for net-zero by 2050 or earlier, companies must embed sustainability, and Singapore can attract green investments through tax breaks, fast-track approvals and a certification one-stop shop.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As Singapore aims for net-zero by 2050 or earlier, companies must embed sustainability into their operations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We would also like to see Singapore positioned as a green hub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We can attract green investments by offering tax breaks for sustainable ventures, fast-track approvals for green projects, a one-stop shop for sustainability certification.

sections.label: SkillsFuture training credits expansion
sections.summary: The SkillsFuture framework should go further by allowing training credits for AI tools, trade association memberships and stipends for reskilling mid-career workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The SkillsFuture framework is a good start, but it must go further – allow training credits to be used for subscribing to AI-powered productivity tools, fund memberships in trade associations and chambers, and business networks that provide continuous learning, provide stipends for mid-career workers undergoing reskilling, not as a support but as a programme.

sections.label: Support for AI-displaced workers
sections.summary: Workers displaced by AI need stronger monthly income support during retraining, tailored career conversion programmes, counselling and mental health support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For those whose jobs that are displaced by AI, we need stronger monthly income support during retraining, career conversion programmes tailored to growth sectors, counselling and mental health support to manage anxiety and uncertainty.

sections.label: R&D grants and business cost relief
sections.summary: The Government must increase R&D grants and tax incentives, create co-funding pools, review regulatory fees and provide targeted relief for SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Government must increase R&D grants and tax incentives, expand the Research and Development Tax Incentive scheme, create co-funding pools for industry-academia collaborations, support proof-of-concept and pilot projects that bridge the gap between lab and market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Businesses are grappling with rising rents, utilities and manpower costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We must review regulatory fees and streamline compliance burdens, provide targeted relief for SMEs in high-cost sectors, ensure housing and transport remain affordable to retain talent.

sections.label: Bridge for trade and excellence
sections.summary: Singapore must be a bridge for trade, become Centres of Excellence, embrace sustainability and prepare its workforce for the AI revolution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We must be the bridge for trade, not a barrier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We must become the Centres of Excellence – in finance, logistics, transport, education, management, medical, sustainability and AI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We must embrace sustainability as a competitive advantage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We must prepare our workforce for the AI revolution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Let us build an economy where every Singaporean can prosper, where every enterprise can grow and where our nation continues to punch above its weight on the global stage. : Allow me to do a pantun on this. :   The changing world brings uncertainties; Singapore companies brace and prepare; Steered by the Government's strategies; Together as one, we forge ahead from there. : Mr Speaker, in conclusion, the Motion before us calls for an economy that is equal, inclusive and driven by dynamic local companies.

sections.label: Shrinking local craft workforce
sections.summary: The local craft workforce has shrunk by 40% to 50%, with only 28% of 186,000 craftsmen and trades workers being locals with a median age of 56.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Over the past decade, the local craft workforce has shrunk by 40% to 50%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Of the 186,000 craftsmen and trades workers in Singapore – only 28% are locals and their ranks are ageing with a median age of 56 years old.

sections.label: Gap between licensed and unregulated trades
sections.summary: Non-compliance carries fines up to $10,000 or three years' jail, yet a massive gap exists between licensed trades persons' rates and unregulated marketplace alternatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While non-compliance carries statutory fines of up to $10,000, a jail term of up to three years, or both, daily practice reveals a massive gap between the rates charged by licensed trades persons and unregulated marketplace alternatives.

sections.label: Water heater electrocution deaths
sections.summary: Improper wiring of water heaters by unlicensed workers caused electrocution deaths of a boy in 2016 and a family in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 2016, the improper wiring of a water heater to a three-pin plug by workers unlicensed to do electrical work resulted in the tragic electrocution of a 15-year-old boy in his HDB flat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Similarly, in 2020, an elderly couple and their son were electrocuted to death in their Jurong flat due to similar unsafe installation of a water heater.

sections.label: Licensing bottleneck and modular endorsement
sections.summary: Post-graduation licensing requires two years of full spectrum practical experience, creating a bottleneck that a modular trade endorsement pathway could resolve.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The structural bottleneck lies in the post-graduation licensing requirements of completing two years of relevant practical experience, covering a full spectrum of trade work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Trade practitioners I spoke to have highlighted that in reality, almost no small contractor covers the entire spectrum of work, expecting a residential service plumber to log experience across industrial supply systems creates a practical bottleneck as current evaluation criteria favour multi-year commercial construction projects over day-to-day residential maintenance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We can resolve the licensing bottleneck by implementing a modular trade endorsement pathway.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Instead of requiring two years of full spectrum experience before a worker can practise independently, this pathway certifies specific verified competencies task by task.

sections.label: Tradesperson skills ledger platform
sections.summary: Operationalising modular endorsements requires a modern digital architecture, an official tradesperson skills ledger platform.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To operationalise these modular endorsements, we need a modern digital architecture, an official tradesperson skills ledger platform.

sections.label: Independent audit for apprentices
sections.summary: An independent audit mechanism is needed if apprentices face unreasonable administrative delays or employer gatekeeping during on-the-job training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While on-the-job training under senior practitioners remains essential, we must ensure that if an apprentice faces unreasonable administrative delays or employer gatekeeping, an independent audit mechanism exists.

sections.label: Support for the Motion
sections.summary: The speaker says the structural redesign will restore workers' leverage and supports the original Motion by Mr Kenneth Tiong and Assoc Prof James Lim.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Through independent representation, technology driven competency tracking and structured apprenticeships, this comprehensive structural redesign will restore our workers' leverage, and ensure that national economic progress serves the dignity and prosperity of every Singaporean.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, I support the original Motion standing in the names of my hon friends, Mr Kenneth Tiong, the Member for Aljunied group representation constituency (GRC), and Assoc Prof James Lim, the Member for Sengkang GRC.

sections.label: ESR engagement numbers
sections.summary: The ESR was informed by more than 80 engagements involving more than 7,700 businesses, workers, unions and trade associations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The ESR was informed by more than 80 engagements involving more than 7,700 businesses, workers, unions and trade associations, some of whom are in this room.

sections.label: Singapore merchandise trade size
sections.summary: In 2025, Singapore's merchandise trade reached almost $1.4 trillion, several times the size of its GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In 2025, Singapore's merchandise trade reached almost $1.4 trillion, equivalent to several times the size of our GDP.

sections.label: EDB investment commitments and jobs
sections.summary: In 2025, EDB secured $14.2 billion in fixed asset investment commitments, expected to create around 15,700 jobs over five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In 2025, EDB secured $14.2 billion in fixed asset investment commitments, with the investment commitments expected to create around 15,700 jobs when realised over the next five years.

sections.label: Private R&D and spillover benefits
sections.summary: Private sector R&D expenditure doubled from $4.3 billion in 2013 to $9 billion in 2023, and a 2025 MTI study estimated spillover benefits from EDB-supported firms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Private sector R&D expenditure more than doubled from $4.3 billion in 2013 to $9 billion in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: A 2025 Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) study estimated that between 2012 and 2019, each EDB-supported firm generated net spillover benefits averaging $48.5 million in value added annually for non-EDB-supported firms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Significantly, this spillover benefits accounted for 41% of the firms' total direct and spillover economic contribution and much of this came through the labour market, as skills and capabilities developed in these firms benefited the wider economy.

sections.label: Capability transfer for workers
sections.summary: The Capability Transfer Programme supports bringing foreign specialists to transfer capabilities to local workers and overseas training for Singaporeans, and more structured transfer could be facilitated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We must help workers move up the same value chain that we want Singapore's economy to move up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We already have the Capability Transfer Programme, supporting companies in bringing foreign specialists to transfer capabilities to our local workforce as well as overseas training for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Could we go further, for example, by facilitating more structured capability transfer from foreign professionals already working here to Singapore colleagues?

sections.label: Labour costs and foreign manpower
sections.summary: The passage asks whether Members are suggesting significantly relaxing foreign manpower policies if labour costs are the principal concern.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: If labour costs are the principal concern, are Members suggesting that we significantly relax our foreign manpower policies?

sections.label: Trade-offs in policy objectives
sections.summary: Parliament has debated proposals on wages, retirement adequacy and environmental measures, which illustrate trade-offs as such measures can affect business cost structures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: At the same time, Parliament has debated proposals before aimed at strengthening wages and retirement adequacy, as well as more ambitious environmental measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: These may be legitimate policy objectives, but they illustrate the trade-offs involved – measures that advance important social or environmental objectives can affect business cost structures So, when we call for lower costs and greater support for local enterprises, I think the next questions should be: what are the concrete policy choices?

sections.label: Committee for Economic Resilience
sections.summary: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs announced the Committee for Economic Resilience, which the speaker co-chairs with Dr Wan Rizal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Within the Malay/Muslim community, the Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs has announced the establishment of the Committee for Economic Resilience, which I co-chair with Dr Wan Rizal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We want to listen to the aspirations and economic concerns of our youths, workers, professionals and entrepreneurs, and help translate the ESR recommendations into more tangible opportunities.

sections.label: AI for Malay/Muslim businesses
sections.summary: The passage asks how more Malay/Muslim business owners can use AI to raise productivity, strengthen competitiveness and grow their businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: How can we help more Malay/Muslim business owners use AI to raise productivity, strengthen competitiveness and grow their businesses?

sections.label: Youths in emerging sectors
sections.summary: The passage asks whether more young people can enter advanced manufacturing, digital technology, AI, the green economy and other emerging sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Can more of our young people enter sectors such as advanced manufacturing, digital technology, AI, the green economy and other emerging sectors?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: These are among the questions that we want to examine through the Committee for Economic Resilience.

sections.label: Motion support with amendments
sections.summary: The speaker cannot support the Motion as it stands but will support it with MP Edward Chia's proposed amendments, including replacing the word "engine".

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Our challenge is to remain global while ensuring that more Singaporeans, businesses and communities participate in the opportunities our global connections create.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: So, Mr Speaker, while I support the aspirations underlying this Motion, I cannot support the Motion as it stands.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I will, however, support the Motion with the proposed amendments by Member of Parliament Mr Edward Chia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: And I will also support, especially the second line, where the word "engine" needs to be replaced, because it is not just a single economic engine.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It is about the whole economy, powered by multiple factors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It makes the second sentence clearer to me.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The amendment may seem minor but it makes it clearer in that sense.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: So, that is, in that sense, with the amendments, how we build stronger companies, create better jobs and build an economy of the future that truly works for all.

sections.label: Redundancy insurance scheme proposal
sections.summary: The passage proposes mandatory retrenchment benefits and a redundancy insurance scheme funded by employer and employee contributions of 0.1% of monthly salary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is a policy choice that unfairly disadvantages our workers and leaves them vulnerable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We must protect hardworking Singaporeans and legislate mandatory retrenchment benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We believe that a redundancy insurance scheme offers better protection for all workers, including our PMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In contrast to the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support scheme, our proposal is meant to be universal and funded by joint contributions from both employers and employees, amounting to a combined 0.1% of the worker's monthly salary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The basic idea is for each retrenched worker to receive 40% of their last drawn salary, which will be further capped at 40% of Singapore's prevailing median income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These payouts will last up to six months at most.

sections.label: Funding for postgraduate reskilling
sections.summary: The passage agrees with ESR Thrust 7 and proposes interest-free education loans and an expanded CPF Education Loan Scheme for postgraduate programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Here, I am in agreement with ESR's diagnosis and recommendation in Thrust 7, which calls for expanding funding support to cover a broader range of deeper rescaling pathways, including post-graduate programmes offered by institutes of higher learning (IHLs).

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, the Government should directly offer mid-career Singaporeans undertaking a postgraduate degree with access to education loans that are interest free for at least the duration of the course and with repayments to start at a modest rate before progressively increasing after a certain period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Second, the Government should expand the CPF Education Loan Scheme to cover part-time and full-time Master's programmes at our IHLs.

sections.label: SWDA integrated support system
sections.summary: SWDA could serve a new integrated system supporting workers through displacement, retraining, job matching and re-employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: SWDA has the potential to serve a new integrated system where workers can be supported actively by the state throughout the entire process of displacement, retraining, job matching and re-employment.

sections.label: SWDA one-stop employment centre
sections.summary: SWDA should be a premier one-stop employment centre assigning each involuntary unemployed jobseeker a dedicated caseworker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: SWDA should serve as a premier one-stop employment centre where every involuntary unemployed jobseeker can be assigned with a dedicated caseworker.

sections.label: Missing workforce development outcome data
sections.summary: Billions support workforce development but little outcome data is public, leaving course, provider, wage and retention outcomes unknown.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We spend billions of dollars supporting workforce development, but surprisingly, little outcome data enters the public domain.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We know, for example, that around 55% of previously unemployed trainees who participated in the SkillsFuture Career Transition Programme found new jobs within six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But we do not know which courses perform better at helping trainees to find new jobs, which providers consistently deliver stronger outcomes, whether wages rise after retraining and whether workers remain employed one year later.

sections.label: Publishing SkillsFuture programme metrics
sections.summary: Government should publish more metrics, such as six-month job placement numbers and average new-job wages per provider and course.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Government should thus publish more metrics to help workers assess the effectiveness of specific SkillsFuture programmes in relation to employment prospects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, for each provider and course, we should publish how many trainees found new jobs within six months and the average wages of these new jobs.

sections.label: AGO finding on grant claim gaming
sections.summary: AGO found six groups of 30-related entities showed patterns suggesting potential gaming of programmes to maximise grant claims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In page 65 of the report, the AGO found that six group of 30-related entities had engaged in patterns that suggested "potential gaming of the programmes to maximise grant claims rather than genuine training initiatives".

sections.label: Course-correction allowance for transfers
sections.summary: Passage asks whether a limited one-time course-correction allowance could disregard one or two subsidised semesters for a first transfer.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: When they transfer programmes, the subsidised semesters already used count against the tuition grant available for the new programme.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Any additional study required may therefore attract non-subsidised fees.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Could there be a limited, one-time course-correction allowance for a first transfer made during the first year?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, one or two subsidised semesters could be disregarded, subject to appropriate academic advising and maximum recognition of credits already completed.

sections.label: Bettr Group coffee training employment
sections.summary: Bettr Group is a homegrown specialty coffee company that combines its business with training and inclusive employment for people facing social and economic barriers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Consider Bettr Group, it is a homegrown specialty coffee company that combines its business with training and inclusive employment for people facing social and economic barriers.

sections.label: Path to develop and progress
sections.summary: Workers should also see a path to develop and progress, building on the ESR's calls for AI to augment workers through job redesign and training.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They should also see a path to develop and progress.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This builds on the ESR, which calls for AI to augment workers through job redesign and training, and for learning to be integrated more closely with real work and employers' needs.

sections.label: Greater responsibilities reflected in pay
sections.summary: Where workers take on greater responsibilities and help generate productivity gains, this should be reflected in their pay or greater autonomy.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Where workers take on greater responsibilities and help generate productivity gains, this should be reflected in their pay or greater autonomy over their work and time.

sections.label: Reciprocal commitment workers and employers
sections.summary: Workers and innovation can flourish together only through a reciprocal commitment, and the speaker would support the Motion as amended by Mr Edward Chia.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Workers and innovation can flourish together, but only through a reciprocal commitment: workers must adapt and employers must create more valuable work and share the gains.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I therefore retain reservations about paragraph (a) as presently framed.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: That said, the amendments proposed by Mr Edward Chia brings the Motion closer to my position and it is more consistent with the points I have made.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And on balance, I would support the Motion as amended.

sections.label: Shorten mandatory retrenchment notification requirement
sections.summary: Thrust 6 calls to shorten the current requirement for companies to submit a mandatory retrenchment notification within five working days after workers are notified.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Thrust 6 makes a specific call to shorten the current requirement for companies to submit a mandatory retrenchment notification within five working days after workers are notified.

sections.label: 4,500 retrenchments April to June
sections.summary: It was reported that the 4,500 retrenchments from April to June this year were the highest since the last quarter of 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Within the story, it was reported that the 4,500 retrenchments from April to June this year were the highest since the last quarter of 2020.

sections.label: Rising recorded retrenchments
sections.summary: Recorded retrenchments rose from 6,440 in 2022 to 13,020 in 2024 and 14,490 in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In this regard, two specific data points are noteworthy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, recorded retrenchments have increased in recent years from 6,440 in 2022 to 13,020 in 2024, and 14,490 in 2025.

sections.label: No statutory retrenchment entitlement
sections.summary: In 2024 potentially close to 3,000 retrenched workers received no benefits or less than the tripartite guidelines, as Singapore workers have no statutory entitlement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Critically, though, what we can reasonably extrapolate from both these data points is that in 2024, for example, potentially close to 3,000 retrenched workers in Singapore either received no retrenchment benefits at all or received less than what is prescribed by the tripartite guidelines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Today, many economies in Asia provide some form of legislative statutory protection for retrenched workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, workers in Singapore have no statutory entitlement to retrenchment benefits.

sections.label: Thailand severance payments law
sections.summary: Thailand legislates severance payments based on years of service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Thailand legislates severance payments based on years of service.

sections.label: DBS financial wellness findings
sections.summary: DBS Bank's 2025 financial wellness series found Gen Zs and Millennials aged 25 to 44 are shouldering heavier liabilities and falling behind in retirement savings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to DBS Bank's 2025 instalment of its financial wellness series, which analysed aggregated and anonymised data from approximately two million DBS and POSB retail customers, Gen Zs and Millennials aged 25 to 44 are increasingly shouldering heavier liabilities and are falling behind their older counterparts in building retirement savings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Among pre-retirement age groups, those aged 35 to 44 are the most financially stretched, with debts slightly overweighing liquid assets, largely due to housing vehicle and credit card loans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: CPF contributions stop, retirement balances grow more slowly, housing obligations continue, healthcare expenses continue, caregiving responsibilities continue.

sections.label: Employers paying retrenchment benefits
sections.summary: Based on available data on retrenchment benefits, many employers are already prepared to pay retrenchment benefits to workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Employers must play their part too, based on the available data on retrenchment benefits, we know that many employers are already prepared to shoulder that responsibility and pay retrenchment benefits to workers.

sections.label: Eight in 10 receive benefits
sections.summary: Eight out of 10 eligible employees already receive retrenchment benefits up to the tripartite guideline of two weeks salary per year of service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Those concerns deserve attention and respect, because it is neither simple nor straightforward to start, build or sustain a business.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, we should not forget that many responsible employers already provide retrenchment benefits: eight out of 10 eligible employees already receive retrenchment benefits up to the tripartite guideline of two weeks salary for every year of service.

sections.label: Subsidiary legislation for higher payouts
sections.summary: Subsidiary legislation could direct higher payouts for larger firms, such as up to one month's salary per year of service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A statutory framework could also be enhanced by subsidiary legislation directing higher payouts for larger firms, such as up to the union norm of one month salary for every year of service, something which larger global MNCs in particular would not necessarily baulk at, especially since they are already subject to legislative regimes governing retrenchment benefits in other countries where they operate.

sections.label: Retrenchment benefit approaches across countries
sections.summary: Some countries create backstops like national insurance, others advance wage guarantee agreements, and others treat retrenchment benefits as preferential debt.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Some create backstops, such as national insurance schemes, while others advance wage guarantee agreements, while yet others treat retrenchment benefits as a preferential debt through insolvency laws.

sections.label: Statutory retrenchment benefits framework call
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to convene employers, unions and workers to develop a statutory retrenchment benefits framework with the objective of introducing legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Trust and commitment to an employer is strengthened when workers know that after years of service, if restructuring occurs through no fault of their own, they will receive fair and meaningful protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Therefore, as part of the Government's implementation of the ESR, I urge the Government to convene employers, unions and workers to develop a statutory retrenchment benefits framework with the objective of introducing legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A resilient society requires workers who know they will not be left to bear the burdens of economic change alone, because in line with the call of the Labour Movement in NTUC, no less, while not every job can be protected, every worker deserves protection.

sections.label: Three factors for worker support
sections.summary: Three sets of factors are needed: nimble workers, transforming organisations, and a refreshed work and learning ecosystem enabled by public policy.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Three sets of factors are needed: first, workers must be nimble and adaptable; second, organisations must transform to activate skills and unlock the potential of workers; third, we need a refreshed work and learning ecosystem enabled by public policy to support workers and organisations, and help them thrive.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development's (OECD's) survey of adult skills suggest that we are only in the middle of the pack relative to OECD economies in adult literacy and numeracy.

sections.label: Formal training not applied at work
sections.summary: Research suggests much of what people learn in formal training is not applied at work due to lack of opportunity or unconducive workplaces.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A body of research, including findings from the Institute for Adult Learning's Skills and Learning Survey, suggests that much of what people learn in formal training is not applied at work, often because there is no opportunity to do so, or because the workplace is not conducive.

sections.label: Roles in enabling learning and skills-first practices
sections.summary: Leaders, HR professionals, line managers and unions have roles in enabling learning, and organisations should adopt skills-first practices for hiring and advancement.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Leaders, human resource (HR) professionals, line managers and unions all have a role to play in enabling learning by activating mindsets, securing training resources, embedding learning and work, and creating conducive environments for learning and experimentation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It should also be a priority for organisations to adopt skills-first practices, where skills, rather than credentials, become the key consideration for hiring, career development and advancement.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This will give employers access to a larger pool of talent, while workers will enjoy greater career mobility as they are not limited by their previous educational qualifications or work experience, but can leverage the skills they have picked up through work to take on new job roles or cross into other sectors.

sections.label: Adult learning skills-first framework
sections.summary: The Institute of Adult Learning will launch a skills-first framework for action in October, setting out actions for individuals, employers and training providers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Institute of Adult Learning will be launching a skills-first framework for action in October, which will set out concrete actions and behaviours that we hope will become widely adopted by individuals, employers and training providers.

sections.label: Skills credentialing for sectors
sections.summary: The Institute of Adult Learning has pioneered skills credentialing for the training and adult education sector and is working with partner agencies to adapt it for other sectors.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Institute of Adult Learning has pioneered skills credentialing for the training and adult education sector, and we are working with partner agencies to adapt this methodology for other sectors.

sections.label: Support for micro entrepreneurship
sections.summary: The Government could review supporting such ventures through financing, AI compute access, business networks, mentoring or other targeted support for micro entrepreneurship.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Government could review what more could be done to support such ventures, whether through financing, access to AI compute, business networks and mentoring, or other targeted forms of support to encourage micro entrepreneurship as a viable career pathway or source of supplementary income for Singaporeans.

sections.label: Lifelong learning and employability expertise
sections.summary: Singapore needs to build expertise in lifelong learning and employability, as it has in pedagogy, to be at the cutting edge in the AI age.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Just as we have built up considerable expertise in pedagogy that has placed Singapore at the forefront of global education for school-age children, we need to similarly build up expertise in lifelong learning and employability.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: By building up our research and practice ecosystem, Singapore can be at the cutting edge of learning and employability in the AI age.

sections.label: ESR members and committees
sections.summary: Of the members and five committees involved in the ESR, it appears to mainly comprise C-suite and NTUC union leaders.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Of the members and five committees involved in the ESR, it appears to mainly comprise C-suite and the NTUC union leaders.

sections.label: Thrust 5 AI-resilient sectors
sections.summary: Thrust 5 of the ESR recommended improving the attractiveness of AI-resilient sectors such as allied health, early childhood education and social work.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In this line, Thrust 5 of the ESR recommended that we improve the attractiveness of AI-resilient sectors, such as allied health, early childhood education and social work.

sections.label: Median wages of nurses, social workers, preschool teachers
sections.summary: MOM data as of June 2025 shows registered nurses earn a median gross wage of $5,129 monthly, social workers $4,565 and preschool teachers $4,150.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Latest MOM data as of June 2025 indicates the median gross wage earned by registered nurses at $5,129 per month.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Social workers earn $4,565, preschool teachers earn $4,150.

sections.label: Burnout study in public healthcare
sections.summary: A 2022 study in the Academy of Medicine, Singapore journal found 37.8% of respondents had high emotional exhaustion, 29.7% high de-personalisation and 55.3% low personal accomplishment.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A 2022 study published in the Academy of Medicine, Singapore's official journal measuring burnout in the public healthcare sector between July 2019 and January 2020 found that 37.8% of respondents had high emotional exhaustion scores; 29.7% had high de-personalisation scores and 55.3% had low personal accomplishment scores.

sections.label: Care economy investment and informal caregiving
sections.summary: The VentureForGood Grant supports social enterprises up to $300,000, and a Duke-NUS study valued informal caregiving for seniors at $1.28 billion annually.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While the current existence of the VentureForGood Grant administered by raiSE SG supports early and growth-stage social enterprises for up to $300,000 in capital expenditure and operating costs, how can we support more startups and commercial enterprises in this space to bring sustainable investments into the care economy? raiSE SG must work with the Ministry of Trade and Industry, and the Ministry of Social and Family Development jointly to review the care economy investment ecosystem to build a more sustainable investment and employment ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Caregiving is also borne by informal carers, such as family and friends.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This labour of love is not reflected in GDP figures, but its importance is underscored by the inaugural Duke-National University of Singapore study, which valued the economic contribution of informal caregiving for seniors at $1.28 billion annually.

sections.label: SME growth stage capital access
sections.summary: The ESR report acknowledges difficulty securing growth stage capital, and suggests ESG work with SGX on governance and disclosure for co-invested companies to ease listing.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For SME looking to scale, the ESR report acknowledges that companies still find it difficult to secure growth stage capital and that Temasek already participates in SME co-investment.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But what our businesses need to grow is bolder and broader base access to financing catalysed by private and public capital.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Enterprise Singapore-co-invested companies, through the Startup SG Equity Scheme, should be re) mainboard or catalyst, and ESG should work with SGX on governance and disclosure requirements for co-invested companies to ease the path to listing.

sections.label: EU second chance policy for entrepreneurs
sections.summary: A 2011 EU expert group report said second chance policies for bankrupt entrepreneurs may be promising, and the EU has adopted a preventive restructuring approach.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A European Union (EU) expert group report in 2011 that, "A second chance policy that enables formally bankrupt entrepreneurs to restart may represent one of the most promising and under-exploited policy options for company creation and job growth." The EU has since adopted a more balanced preventive restructuring approach for bona fide entrepreneurs seeking a second chance.

sections.label: Data centres moving to Johor and Batam
sections.summary: The 2019 moratorium on new data centres and higher operating costs drove operators to Johor and Batam, with Singaporean companies owning the largest capacity share there.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The earlier 2019 moratorium on new data centres, as well as higher operating costs here, drove operators to set up shop in neighbouring Johor and Batam, with Singaporean companies owning the largest proportion of data centre capacity in both regions.

sections.label: Forest clearing and resource use
sections.summary: Forests are being cleared for housing and a commercial hub, while electricity and non-domestic water consumption are rising.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Concern is mounting over forests being cut down for housing, both at Maju Forest and Gillman Barracks, alongside a patch of forest near Woodlands Checkpoint, which would be cleared for the development of a new commercial hub, while over 52 hectares of forested land would be cut down for the next phase of the Jurong Innovation District.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: EMA noted that electricity consumption increased by 4% year-on-year in 2024, with commerce and service-related businesses consuming the highest proportion that year at 40.2% of our total electricity use.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Already, non-domestic water consumption takes up 55% of our total water use and PUB estimates that this is expected to increase to 60% by 2065.

sections.label: AI disrupting jobs
sections.summary: AI will disrupt jobs at a speed and scale not seen before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: AI will disrupt jobs at a speed and scale that we have not seen before.

sections.label: Retrenchment benefits and unemployment support
sections.summary: NTUC and tripartite partners are working to ensure no worker is left behind on retrenchment benefits and unemployment support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: There are two topics in this space, firstly, on retrenchment benefits and unemployment support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: And on the topic of mandating retrenchment benefits, the NTUC and the Labour Movement, including myself, have been working with tripartite partners to ensure that no worker is left behind.

sections.label: Strengthening retrenchment protection regime
sections.summary: Tripartite partners are negotiating whether to review the Employment Act and strengthen advisories into guidelines with stronger measures against non-compliant companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In fact, we have been trying to lobby, myself inclusive, in this House, for the past decade, including earlier this year, for further strengthening of the retrenchment protection regime here in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In fact, the tripartite partners, as I am involved in the negotiations for the Employment Act as well as all the relevant statutory provisions as well as advisories, we remain open in negotiating and discussions are underway, whether it is the Employment Act reviewing the Tripartite Advisory to strengthen it to tripartite guidelines, which I have raised before in this House, and even stronger measures against companies that flopped or failed to, comply with advisories.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support Scheme
sections.summary: The SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support Scheme was implemented on 26 April last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: On the topic of unemployment insurance support, this is something I spoke about more than a decade ago, lobbying for some form of unemployment support for workers in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I am very happy that it has been introduced last year, on 26 April – I remember the fateful date – the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support Scheme was implemented.

sections.label: Raising Jobseeker Support income threshold
sections.summary: With more PMEs affected by lay-offs, the income threshold of the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support scheme, currently $5,000, could be raised to the median salary of PMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: And I have, at the same time, in this same House, also lobbied for this area to be further expanded and rebuilt, now that we are seeing in the last 24 months more PMEs being affected by lay-offs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: So, that is an area which we can review, whether the income threshold of the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support scheme can be raised – because currently, that is $5,000 – whether it can be raised to the median salary of PMEs, so, that is one avenue to explore.

sections.label: Tripartite Jobs Council formation
sections.summary: MOM, NTUC and the Singapore National Employers Federation announced the formation of the Tripartite Jobs Council earlier this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Earlier this year, MOM, NTUC and Singapore National Employers Federation announced the formation of the Tripartite Jobs Council.

sections.label: ESR Committees engagement numbers

sentences.text: Five ESR Committees engaged more than 7,700 people over nine months.

sections.label: MNCs and SMEs both needed

sections.label: Grants and loans for SMEs

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Every year, the Government provides nearly $2 billion dollars in direct grants and loans for our local SMEs to build stronger capabilities, embark on new projects and compete successfully in global markets.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: We can do more to help our companies make fuller use of the support available.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: And if demand for these schemes grows because more companies are stepping up and making use of them, let me state for the record that the Ministry of Finance stands ready in support with more resources.

sections.label: Enterprise Singapore supporting local companies

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: That is why in 2018, we re-organised agencies in MTI to form Enterprise Singapore – a new Statutory Board with a clear mission to support our local companies end-to-end: capability building, innovation, financing, talent, internationalisation.

sentences.text: This is why it is important that the ESR is a whole-of-society effort, led by a new generation of business, union, society and Government leaders, who will collectively own these outcomes.
